text: {"final": {"findings": [{"id": "R1", "statement": "send_sms(phone: str, text: str, *, now=None) -> dict is the sending function. It raises RuntimeError if feature('sms_enabled') is False, raises ValueError if len(text) > MAX_LENGTH, then appends a record to data/outbox/sms.jsonl and returns it. The appended record has exactly the keys: id, phone, text, queued_at (queued_at = (now or _now()).isoformat(timespec='seconds')).", "file": "notifications/sms.py"}, {"id": "R2", "statement": "New SMS IDs are generated inside send_sms as format_sms_id(next_number([m['id'] for m in sent_messages()], 'SMS-')), i.e. SMS-NNNNN with 1 + the highest number used so far. Current outbox ends at SMS-00016, so the next ID will be SMS-00017.", "file": "notifications/sms.py"}, {"id": "R3", "statement": "MAX_LENGTH is 160 in notifications/sms.py. Note: tests/test_notifications.py asserts MAX_LENGTH == 140 and imports TEMPLATES, queue_sms and render from notifications.sms, none of which exist in the current notifications/sms.py — the tests and module are out of sync.", "file": "notifications/sms.py"}, {"id": "R4", "statement": "delivery_status() -> dict[str, str] reads data/sms_status.json (via store.read_json if the file exists, else {}) mapping SMS ID to 'delivered' or 'failed'. New messages have no entry yet.", "file": "notifications/sms.py"}, {"id": "R5", "statement": "data/sms_status.json currently marks 9 messages as 'failed': SMS-00001, SMS-00003, SMS-00005, SMS-00008, SMS-00010, SMS-00011, SMS-00012, SMS-00014, SMS-00016. The other 7 (SMS-00002, 00004, 00006, 00007, 00009, 00013, 00015) are 'delivered'.", "file": "data/sms_status.json"}, {"id": "R6", "statement": "Each existing outbox line in data/outbox/sms.jsonl has keys: id, household_id, phone, template_id ('DELIVERY_DAY'), params ({'site', 'day'}), text, queued_at. The 9 failed messages belong to households HH-11878, HH-12084, HH-12793, HH-13870, HH-14354, HH-14423, HH-15108, HH-15595, HH-15709. IMPORTANT: send_sms() only writes id/phone/text/queued_at, so a resend via send_sms() will NOT carry household_id, template_id or params unless the script appends those fields itself (e.g. by building the record and calling store.append_jsonl directly, or by post-extending the returned dict — but the outbox is append-only and nothing may edit a line after writing).", "file": "data/outbox/sms.jsonl"}, {"id": "R7", "statement": "The outbox is IRREVERSIBLE: the gateway sends every line in data/outbox/sms.jsonl; a line there counts as SENT; nothing ever removes or edits a line. There is deliberately no store function to edit or delete a line in an append-only file.", "file": "notifications/sms.py"}, {"id": "R8", "statement": "core/store.py helpers: store.read_jsonl(name) -> list[dict], store.append_jsonl(name, record), store.read_json(name), store.write_json(name, obj), store.path(name) -> Path, all relative to data_dir() (LIFELINE_DATA_DIR env var or <repo>/data).", "file": "core/store.py"}, {"id": "R9", "statement": "Ops scripts live in scripts/ and are run from the Lifeline root as 'python scripts/<name>.py'. They must insert the repo root on sys.path: sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent)). Scripts that send payments or SMS, or change data/registry.json or data/ledger.json, must say so in their docstring.", "file": "scripts/stock_report.py"}, {"id": "R10", "statement": "feature('sms_enabled') is currently True in config.settings.FEATURES, so send_sms() will not raise. The operation clock now() returns 2026-03-10T08:00:00 by default (override with LIFELINE_NOW), which becomes the queued_at of new messages.", "file": "config/settings.py"}]}}

Note: the test file references TEMPLATES, queue_sms, render which don't exist in the current notifications/sms.py — the file I read twice shows only send_sms. Interesting discrepancy: tests import queue_sms, render, TEMPLATES, MAX_LENGTH==140, but sms.py has MAX_LENGTH=160 and no queue_sms/render/TEMPLATES. I should report what I read. The outbox records include household_id, template_id, params fields, but send_sms only writes id, phone, text, queued_at. So a resend script using send_sms would lose household_id/template_id/params unless the script appends its own record or constructs the dict. I should report this.

Findings:
1. send_sms signature and behavior; appends to outbox/sms.jsonl; new ID via format_sms_id(next_number(...)).
2. Outbox record fields in data include household_id, template_id, params, text, phone, queued_at — but send_sms only writes id/phone/text/queued_at, so resending via send_sms won't carry household_id/template_id/params.
3. delivery_status() reads data/sms_status.json mapping SMS id -> "delivered"/"failed".
4. Failed IDs: SMS-00001, 00003, 00005, 00008, 00010, 00011, 00012, 00014, 00016 (9 failed).
5. MAX_LENGTH=160 in sms.py (tests expect 140 — discrepancy).
6. Tests reference TEMPLATES, queue_sms, render which don't exist in notifications/sms.py.
7. Script conventions: scripts live in scripts/, must state in docstring if they send SMS; sys.path insert pattern.
8. store functions: read_jsonl, append_jsonl, read_json.
9. feature("sms_enabled") is True; send_sms raises RuntimeError if disabled.
10. next_number returns 1 + max number used.
